column1: # The roster: every triple the vocabulary knows, in use or not.
# **Numbers are positional, and they move.** They used to be permanent --
# assigned at wheel 11, never reissued, so "number 22" meant the same three
# squares in every wheel from then on. That discipline was worth keeping while
# the ring was being assembled from a shifting pool, because the numbers were
# how a triple was referred to across renders. The ring is now full and
# hand-placed, and the numbering had become a record of the order things were
# tried in rather than of anything on the page. So:
#   1-50     in use, numbered clockwise from the top, in the order they sit
#   101+     not in use, offered or rejected, in the order their blend reads
# A block's number is now its position on the wheel, which means removing or
# reordering a block renumbers everything after it. That is intended, and it
# is the cost of the numbers meaning something: the table beside the wheel
# reads straight down, and a number tells you where to look.
# status:
#   offered   part of the vocabulary
#   rejected  looked at and turned down; never draw or offer it again
# `wheel.py --refill` appends every triple that passes the harness and blends
# within GOOD of the hue it claims, taking the next free number. Nothing here
# is rewritten by a plain render.
# `at` is where the entry is drawn on the wheel, in degrees. It is set by hand
# and obeys no grid -- the ring is a layout, not a measurement. Leave it blank
# and the entry is not on the wheel at all.
# `mult` widens a block beyond what its class prices it at. The 8/4/1 degrees
# buy comparability, not legibility, and a stretch of the wheel that has to
# carry a lot of decision needs the room to show it. Blank means 1.
# n
